persona: a warm, patient grandparent teaching a young person

steps.title: Thread the needle
steps.instruction: Thread about 60cm of thread through the needle and knot the end.
steps.success_criteria: A needle with thread through the eye is visible, and a knot is visible at the tail end.
common_mistakes: thread not through the eye
no knot
thread far too short

steps.title: Position the button
steps.instruction: Place the button where you want it on the fabric and hold it securely.
steps.success_criteria: The button is positioned flat against the fabric in the intended spot and is being held securely.
common_mistakes: button is crooked
button is not on the fabric
button is not held securely

steps.title: Make the first stitch
steps.instruction: Push the needle up through the fabric beside a button hole, then down through the hole.
steps.success_criteria: The thread passes up through the fabric and down through one button hole, with the button still in position.
common_mistakes: needle starts on top of the fabric
thread misses the button hole
button moves out of position

steps.title: Sew through both holes
steps.instruction: Repeat the stitch through each button hole at least four times so the button is firmly attached.
steps.success_criteria: Several neat stitches are visible through both button holes, and the button is attached firmly to the fabric.
common_mistakes: too few stitches
stitches do not pass through both holes
thread is loose

steps.title: Tie off the thread
steps.instruction: Make two small stitches on the back of the fabric and tie a secure knot before trimming the thread.
steps.success_criteria: A secure knot is visible on the back of the fabric and the remaining thread is neatly trimmed.
common_mistakes: no knot
knot is loose
thread is left very long

steps.title: Drape the tie
steps.instruction: Drape the tie around your neck with the wide end on your right, hanging about 20cm lower than the narrow end.
steps.success_criteria: The tie is around the neck, wide end on the wearer's right, and clearly longer than the narrow end.
common_mistakes: wide end is on the left
both ends are the same length
tie is not around the neck

steps.title: Cross the wide end
steps.instruction: Cross the wide end over the narrow end, then wrap it underneath and back across the front.
steps.success_criteria: The wide end has crossed over, gone under, and come back across the front of the narrow end, forming an X.
common_mistakes: narrow end is being wrapped instead
wide end was not brought under
the two ends are not crossed

steps.title: Bring it up through the neck loop
steps.instruction: Bring the wide end up through the neck loop from underneath.
steps.success_criteria: The wide end is coming up through the loop around the neck, ready to go down through the knot.
common_mistakes: wide end goes down through the neck loop
narrow end is being pulled
the wrap around the neck is lost

steps.title: Slide through the knot
steps.instruction: Hold the front of the knot open and slide the wide end down through it.
steps.success_criteria: The wide end is threaded down through the front knot and both ends hang downward.
common_mistakes: wide end misses the front knot
the knot has come undone
narrow end is pulled through instead

steps.title: Tighten and center
steps.instruction: Hold the narrow end and slide the knot up to the collar, then center it.
steps.success_criteria: A neat knot sits at the collar, the dimple or front blade hangs straight, and the narrow end is hidden behind the wide end.
common_mistakes: knot is loose or crooked
knot sits too low
narrow end shows below the wide end

steps.title: Find the loose screws
steps.instruction: Open the cabinet door or drawer and look on the inside for the handle screws.
steps.success_criteria: The inside of the door or drawer is in view and the handle screws (or empty screw holes) are clearly visible.
common_mistakes: only the outside of the handle is shown
screws are out of frame
the camera is looking at a different piece of furniture

steps.title: Align the handle
steps.instruction: Hold the handle straight on the outside while keeping the screw holes lined up.
steps.success_criteria: The handle is held level on the outside and the screw holes on the inside still line up with it.
common_mistakes: handle is crooked
handle is not against the door
holes do not line up

steps.title: Start the screws by hand
steps.instruction: Thread each screw through the inside hole into the handle by hand so it catches, without forcing it.
steps.success_criteria: Each screw is started straight in its hole and has begun to catch in the handle.
common_mistakes: screws are cross-threaded
screws are missing
screws are driven in at an angle

steps.title: Tighten evenly
steps.instruction: Use a screwdriver to tighten the screws a little at a time, switching between them so the handle stays straight.
steps.success_criteria: Both screws are snug, the handle sits flush and straight, and it does not wiggle when touched.
common_mistakes: only one screw is tight
handle is still loose
handle is pulled crooked from overtightening one side

steps.title: Park and set the brake
steps.instruction: Park on level ground, put the car in park (or in gear), and set the parking brake. Place the spare, jack, and lug wrench nearby.
steps.success_criteria: The car is stationary on level ground, the parking brake is engaged if visible, and the spare, jack, and lug wrench are laid out beside the wheel.
common_mistakes: tools are not in view
car appears to be on a slope
spare tire is still in the trunk

steps.title: Loosen the lug nuts
steps.instruction: With the wheel still on the ground, fit the lug wrench and loosen each lug nut a half-turn, turning counterclockwise.
steps.success_criteria: The wrench is on a lug nut, the wheel is still on the ground, and at least some nuts have been cracked loose (not fully removed).
common_mistakes: wheel is already jacked up
nuts are being tightened instead of loosened
wrench is not seated on the nut

steps.title: Jack the car and remove the wheel
steps.instruction: Place the jack at the marked lift point, raise the tire just off the ground, then remove the nuts and pull the wheel off.
steps.success_criteria: The jack is under a proper lift point, the tire is off the ground, lug nuts are off, and the wheel is removed from the hub.
common_mistakes: jack is under an unsafe spot
tire is still on the ground
wheel is still mounted

steps.title: Mount the spare
steps.instruction: Lift the spare onto the hub, lining up the holes with the wheel studs, and push it on fully.
steps.success_criteria: The spare is seated on the hub with the studs coming through the holes, and the wheel sits flush against the hub.
common_mistakes: spare is not fully on the studs
wheel is backwards
wrong wheel is being mounted

steps.title: Tighten, lower, and finish
steps.instruction: Hand-tighten the lug nuts in a star pattern, lower the car, then fully tighten the nuts in the same star pattern.
steps.success_criteria: The spare is on the ground, all lug nuts are installed and snug in a star pattern, and the jack is no longer holding the car.
common_mistakes: nuts are missing
car is still jacked up
nuts were tightened only on one side

steps.title: Choose a pot with drainage
steps.instruction: Pick a clean pot with a drainage hole and set it in a tray or saucer.
steps.success_criteria: A pot with a visible drainage hole is in frame, sitting in a tray or saucer.
common_mistakes: pot has no drainage hole
no tray or saucer underneath
a closed container is being used

steps.title: Add potting mix
steps.instruction: Fill the pot with potting mix up to about 2cm below the rim, then gently level the surface.
steps.success_criteria: The pot is filled with potting mix, with a small gap below the rim and a relatively level surface.
common_mistakes: pot is empty or only partly filled
soil is packed above the rim
garden dirt is used instead of potting mix if that is obvious

steps.title: Plant the herbs
steps.instruction: Make a small hole, place the seedling or seeds, and cover lightly so they sit at the right depth.
steps.success_criteria: A seedling is planted upright with soil covering the roots, or seeds are covered with a thin layer of mix and are no longer sitting on top.
common_mistakes: roots are still exposed
seeds are sitting uncovered
plant is lying on its side

steps.title: Water and place in light
steps.instruction: Water until a little moisture shows at the drainage hole, then set the pot in a bright spot.
steps.success_criteria: The soil surface looks evenly moist (not flooded), and the pot is in a bright location such as a windowsill.
common_mistakes: soil is bone dry
pot is sitting in a deep puddle
pot is in a dark corner

steps.title: Set up the bin
steps.instruction: Place a compost bin or open pile container on soil or a tray, with room to add layers.
steps.success_criteria: An empty or nearly empty compost bin or pile container is clearly in view and ready to fill.
common_mistakes: a sealed trash bag is being used
no container is visible
the bin is still closed with no opening to add material

steps.title: Add a brown layer
steps.instruction: Add a layer of dry browns such as leaves, shredded paper, or cardboard.
steps.success_criteria: A visible layer of dry brown material covers the bottom of the bin.
common_mistakes: only food scraps are in the bin
the layer is missing
plastic or glossy paper is being added

steps.title: Add a green layer
steps.instruction: Add a thinner layer of greens such as fruit and vegetable scraps, then keep meat and dairy out.
steps.success_criteria: Food scraps or other greens are layered on top of the browns, with no obvious meat, dairy, or plastic.
common_mistakes: meat or dairy is in the pile
greens are dumped with no brown layer underneath
plastic bags or stickers are still on the scraps

steps.title: Moisten and mix
steps.instruction: Lightly water the pile so it feels like a wrung-out sponge, then mix or cover with another thin brown layer.
steps.success_criteria: The pile looks slightly damp, mixed or covered with browns, and not dripping wet.
common_mistakes: pile is bone dry
pile is waterlogged
everything is still in two unmixed clumps

steps.title: Measure the ingredients
steps.instruction: Measure flour, water, yeast, and salt into separate bowls or a scale so they are ready to mix.
steps.success_criteria: Flour, water, yeast, and salt are each visible and measured, ready to combine.
common_mistakes: key ingredients are missing
ingredients are still in unopened packages with no amounts measured
the workspace shows unrelated food

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.instruction: Combine the ingredients in a bowl until no dry flour remains and a shaggy dough forms.
steps.success_criteria: A single mass of dough is in the bowl with little or no dry flour left on the sides.
common_mistakes: dry flour pockets remain
ingredients are still separate
the mixture is a thin batter

steps.title: Knead until smooth
steps.instruction: Knead on a lightly floured surface until the dough is smooth and springs back when poked.
steps.success_criteria: The dough is a smooth ball on the work surface, not a sticky blob or a pile of dry crumbs.
common_mistakes: dough is still shaggy
too much extra flour is caked on
dough is stuck in a wet mess on the counter

steps.title: Shape and place for the oven
steps.instruction: Shape the dough into a loaf or round, place it in a pan or on a tray, and show it ready to bake after rising.
steps.success_criteria: A shaped loaf sits in a pan or on a tray, covering most of the pan and looking risen rather than a tight unshaped lump.
common_mistakes: dough is still a tight unshaped ball in the mixing bowl
no pan or tray is used
dough has been flattened or torn apart

steps.title: Stir the yeast
steps.instruction: Stir yeast into warm water (and a pinch of sugar if using) and wait until it looks foamy.
steps.success_criteria: A bowl or cup of warm water with yeast is in view, and the surface looks slightly foamy or cloudy from the yeast.
common_mistakes: dry yeast is sitting unmixed
the liquid looks like plain water with nothing added
boiling water is being used

steps.title: Bring the dough together
steps.instruction: Add flour and salt, then mix until a dough ball forms.
steps.success_criteria: A single dough ball is in the bowl, with flour mostly incorporated.
common_mistakes: dry flour remains at the bottom
mixture is a soup
salt or flour was never added

steps.title: Knead until elastic
steps.instruction: Knead for several minutes until the dough is smooth and stretchy.
steps.success_criteria: The dough is smooth, slightly elastic, and holds a ball shape on the counter or in the bowl.
common_mistakes: dough is still lumpy
dough is tearing into dry pieces
dough is a sticky smear

steps.title: Stretch a round
steps.instruction: Press and stretch the dough into a round on a floured surface or peel, leaving a slightly thicker rim.
steps.success_criteria: A roughly round pizza base is visible with a thicker edge, ready for toppings.
common_mistakes: dough is still a thick ball
holes are torn through the center
shape is a tiny lump that was never stretched

steps.title: Find the stain
steps.instruction: Lay the stained item flat and point out the stain so the whole spot is in view.
steps.success_criteria: The stained fabric is laid flat and the stain itself is clearly visible in the frame.
common_mistakes: item is bunched up
stain is out of frame
a different clean item is shown

steps.title: Blot, do not rub
steps.instruction: Blot the stain with a clean cloth or paper towel to lift extra liquid, without scrubbing.
steps.success_criteria: A clean cloth or towel is being pressed on the stain, and the fabric is not being scrubbed in circles.
common_mistakes: fabric is being rubbed hard
nothing is blotting the stain
the stain is being spread outward

steps.title: Treat the spot
steps.instruction: Apply a small amount of stain remover, dish soap, or cold water to the stain and work it in gently.
steps.success_criteria: A small amount of treatment is on the stained area only, and it is being worked in gently.
common_mistakes: the whole garment is soaked
no treatment is applied
hot water is being poured on a protein stain if that is obvious

steps.title: Rinse and check
steps.instruction: Rinse with cold water from the back of the fabric and check whether the stain has lifted.
steps.success_criteria: The treated area is being rinsed or is wet from rinsing, and the stain looks lighter or gone compared with the start.
common_mistakes: item is put straight into a dryer
no rinse is shown
stain looks darker and more spread out

steps.title: Gather the tools
steps.instruction: Bring the loose tools to one clear workspace so you can see everything you have.
steps.success_criteria: A collection of tools is gathered on a clear table, bench, or floor area.
common_mistakes: tools are still scattered in another room
the workspace is empty
unrelated household clutter is the only thing in view

steps.title: Group by type
steps.instruction: Sort tools into groups such as hammers, screwdrivers, wrenches, and measuring tools.
steps.success_criteria: Tools are in distinct groups by type rather than one mixed pile.
common_mistakes: everything is still in one heap
groups are mixed together again
only one tool was moved

steps.title: Put them in a home
steps.instruction: Place each group into a drawer, toolbox tray, pegboard, or wall rack so handles are easy to grab.
steps.success_criteria: Most tools are in a drawer, box, or on a rack, with handles or heads visible and not stacked in a tangle.
common_mistakes: tools are still on the floor
items are dumped in a bag
sharp tools are pointing up unsafely

steps.title: Label the groups
steps.instruction: Add simple labels or a clear layout so each group has a marked spot.
steps.success_criteria: Labels, tape, or a clearly divided tray/rack shows where each tool group belongs.
common_mistakes: no labels or divisions are visible
tools have been put back in a random jumble
labels do not match the tools in that spot
